title: Reply to Ranger Fern
task: Read the email from Ranger Fern and the notes you have made. Write your email to Fern using all the notes. Write about 100 words.

email.text: Hi! Thanks for volunteering for the Lantern Festival clean-up next Saturday. Would you prefer to collect rubbish or decorate the trees? Could you bring anything? We start at 9 am. Is that OK for you?

model:
Hi Fern,

Thanks for your email! I'm really excited about the clean-up because I've never done anything like this before.

I'd prefer to decorate the trees, as I love making things and I'm quite good at climbing. If you want, I can bring some paper lanterns and a big bag of fairy lights from home.

Starting at 9 am is fine for me, but I might be a few minutes late because the first forest bus only arrives at 8.55.

See you on Saturday!
Best wishes,
Mia

It was great to hear from you.

title: Your Pen Friend Is Coming!
task: Read the email from your pen friend Arlo and the notes you have made. Write your email to Arlo using all the notes. Write about 100 words.

email.text: Great news: I'm coming to visit your town next month! What should I see while I'm there? What should I pack? And could we go somewhere special together?

model:
Hi Arlo,

It's fantastic news that you're coming! I can't wait to show you my town.

You should definitely visit the old castle on the hill, because the view from the tower is amazing. The flower market on Sunday mornings is lovely too.

The weather here changes quickly, so don't forget to pack an umbrella and a warm jacket.

Why don't we take the little boat to the Whispering Islands? I've been there twice and it's the most magical place I know.

Let me know when you arrive!
Best wishes,
Noor

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: The Old Wooden Box
task: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence: “As soon as Mia opened the old wooden box, the forest went completely silent.” Write about 100 words.
firstLine: As soon as Mia opened the old wooden box, the forest went completely silent.
model:
As soon as Mia opened the old wooden box, the forest went completely silent. Inside, there was a tiny golden key and a note that said: "Give me back my song."

Suddenly, Mia realised that all the birds had stopped singing. She was scared, but she decided to follow the path to the oldest tree. There, she found a small door with a lock.

Mia turned the key and hundreds of songs flew out like butterflies. In the end, the whole forest was singing again, and from that day on the birds always sang a little louder near Mia's house.

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: My Favourite Place to Relax
task: You see this notice in the Forest Gazette: “Articles wanted! Where is your favourite place to relax? What do you do there? Why is it special to you?” Write your article in about 100 words.
model:
The Secret Willow

Have you ever wanted to hide from the world for an hour? My favourite place to relax is under an old willow tree by the river, just ten minutes from my house.

When I get there, I usually sit on its roots, listen to the water and read a good book. Sometimes I draw the ducks that swim past.

What makes it special is the quiet. Nobody can find me there, so I always feel calm and peaceful. I've been going there since I was little, and it still feels like my own secret world.

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: Advice for a Nervous Friend
task: Read the email from your friend Jade and the notes you have made. Write your email to Jade using all the notes. Write about 100 words.

email.text: I've got my first big exam next week and I'm so nervous! Have you got any advice? How do you relax before exams? Do you think I should study all night?

model:
Hi Jade,

Don't worry, it's completely normal to feel nervous before a big exam! If I were you, I'd make a simple plan and revise a little every day.

Before exams, I usually go for a walk in the forest or listen to some calm music. It really helps me relax.

Please don't study all night! You won't remember much if you're tired. It's much better to go to bed early and have a good breakfast in the morning.

Good luck! I'm sure you'll do brilliantly.
Love,
Sam

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: The Owl's Secret Message
task: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence: “When Leo heard a tap on his window at midnight, he couldn't believe his eyes.” Write about 100 words.
firstLine: When Leo heard a tap on his window at midnight, he couldn't believe his eyes.

points.label: How Leo felt at the end

model:
When Leo heard a tap on his window at midnight, he couldn't believe his eyes. A snowy owl was sitting there with a tiny letter in its beak.

The message said: "The moon has fallen into the lake. Please help!" Without thinking, Leo put on his coat and followed the owl through the dark forest.

At the lake, the moon was floating like a giant pearl. Leo pushed it gently with a long branch until it rose back into the sky.

When he got home, he felt tired but incredibly proud, and he smiled all the way to bed.

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: My Favourite Hobby
task: You see this notice in an English magazine for teenagers: “Articles wanted! What is your favourite hobby? How did you start it? Why should other people try it?” Write your article in about 100 words.
model:
Why Not Try Baking?

My favourite hobby is baking, and I spend most Saturday afternoons in the kitchen. I started when I was nine, because my grandma taught me how to make her famous lemon cake. At first my cakes were flat and burnt, but I kept practising.

Now I can bake bread, cookies and even birthday cakes for my friends. Baking is relaxing, and you can eat the results!

If you have never tried it, why not start with something simple, like banana muffins? You will be surprised how easy it is.

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: Plans for the Class Trip
task: Read the email from your English teacher Ms Rivera and the notes you have made. Write your email to Ms Rivera using all the notes. Write about 100 words.

email.text: Our class is going on a trip at the end of term! Would you prefer to visit the science museum or the zoo? What would you like to do there? Also, could you help me with something on the day?

points.label: Explain what you'd like to do
Offer to help and say how

model:
Dear Ms Rivera,

Thank you for your email. I think the science museum would be better than the zoo, because we went to the zoo last year.

I'd like to see the space gallery, because there is a real moon rock there. It would also be fun to try the experiments in the hands-on room.

Of course I can help on the day! I could carry the first-aid bag or count everyone on the coach. I'm happy to do anything you need.

Best wishes,
Sam

title: The Map in the Library Book
task: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence: “When Maya opened the library book, a small map fell out.” Write about 100 words.
firstLine: When Maya opened the library book, a small map fell out.
model:
When Maya opened the library book, a small map fell out. It showed the school garden, with a red cross under the old apple tree.

After lessons, while it was getting dark, Maya and her friend Tom took a spade and started to dig. Although they were tired, they kept going. Suddenly, the spade hit something hard. It was a rusty tin box!

Inside they found old photos and a letter from a girl who studied at the school fifty years ago. The next day they showed the head teacher, so now everyone can see the treasure.

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: Which Pet Should We Get?
task: Read the email from your friend Priya and the notes you have made. Write your email to Priya using all the notes. Write about 100 words.

email.text: Guess what? My parents say we can get a pet! Which pet do you think we should get? How should we look after it? And would you like to come and meet it?

points.label: Explain how to look after it

model:
Hi Priya,

That's brilliant news! I think you should get a guinea pig, because they are friendly and very quiet. I've had one for two years, and she has never bitten anyone.

You will need to feed it fresh vegetables and hay every day, and also clean its cage once a week. If you play with it every evening, it will soon learn your voice.

I'd love to come and meet your new pet! Could I visit next Saturday?

Love,
Emma

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: The Best Day Out in My Town
task: You see this notice in an English magazine for teenagers: “Articles wanted! What is the best day out in your town? What can you do there? Why should visitors go?” Write your article in about 100 words.
model:
A Day at Riverside Park

If you only have one day in my town, the best day out is Riverside Park. It is right next to the river, just ten minutes from the station.

You can hire a little boat, feed the ducks or climb the giant rope pyramid. My favourite part is the wildflower maze, where you can easily get lost!

Visitors should go because almost everything is free, and the café sells the best strawberry pancakes I have ever tasted. Why not take a picnic and stay until sunset? You will not be disappointed.

p: If you only have one day in …
It was great to hear from you.

title: Welcome to Our School
task: Read the email from your new pen friend Leo and the notes you have made. Write your email to Leo using all the notes. Write about 100 words.

email.text: Great news: I'm starting at your school next month! What are the teachers like? Which clubs do you think I should join? And what should I bring on my first day?

points.label: Say what the teachers are like

model:
Hi Leo,

That's brilliant news! I'm sure you will love our school. Most of the teachers are really friendly, although the maths teacher is a bit strict about homework.

I think you should join the robotics club, because you told me you love building things. We meet on Wednesdays and we're making a robot that can dance!

On your first day, don't forget to bring a pencil case, a water bottle and a packed lunch, because the canteen is closed on Mondays. I'll wait for you at the main gate.

See you soon,
Alex

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: The Robot in the Attic
task: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence: “As soon as Ben switched on the old robot, its eyes began to glow.” Write about 100 words.
firstLine: As soon as Ben switched on the old robot, its eyes began to glow.
model:
As soon as Ben switched on the old robot, its eyes began to glow. It had been in Grandpa's attic for years.

Suddenly, it spoke in a squeaky voice: "Hello, Ben! Shall I tidy your room?" Ben couldn't believe his ears. Before he could answer, the robot rolled downstairs and started folding all the laundry.

Grandpa laughed. He explained that he had built the robot when he was a boy, but it had stopped working.

From that day on, Ben and the robot did their chores together, and they always finished in time to play.

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: Ideas for a Greener School
task: Read the email from your teacher Mr Patel and the notes you have made. Write your email to Mr Patel using all the notes. Write about 100 words.

email.text: We want to make our school greener this year. What is one change we could make? How could students help? Would you like to join the new eco team?

points.label: Say yes to the eco team

model:
Dear Mr Patel,

Thank you for asking for our ideas. I think we could plant a vegetable garden next to the playground. It would be good for bees and butterflies, and the canteen could use the vegetables.

Students could help by watering the plants at break time, and each class could look after its own bed. We could also collect rainwater in big barrels, so we do not waste water from the taps.

I would love to join the new eco team! I am free on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.

Best wishes,
Hana

p: It was great to hear from you.

title: The Noise in the Shed
task: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence: “Lucy heard a strange noise coming from the garden shed.” Write about 100 words.
firstLine: Lucy heard a strange noise coming from the garden shed.
model:
Lucy heard a strange noise coming from the garden shed. It sounded like someone was snoring! At first, she thought it was her little brother, but he was inside.

Slowly, she opened the door and switched on her torch. To her surprise, she found a hedgehog curled up in an old flowerpot, with three tiny babies next to her.

Lucy did not want to scare them, so she quietly left a dish of water and some cat food by the door.

In the end, the hedgehog family stayed all winter, and Lucy visited them every evening.

p: It was great to hear from you.
